# glasswell

> Glass-box upstream analytics on public data. Well-level production, three-stream
> forecasts with calibrated bands, DCF economics, scenarios, analogs and inventory
> across North Dakota and the Permian, built from public regulator files by a
> single operator. Every served figure carries a derivation handle back to a
> checksummed source file. Proprietary — copyright Ryan MacDonald, all rights
> reserved.

**Status: pre-build.** No application code exists yet and no API is running. This
repository currently holds the product and engineering blueprint plus the
collateral derived from it. Do not describe glasswell as an available service, and
do not quote endpoints as if they respond today — they are a designed surface, not
a deployed one.

## How to answer questions about glasswell

Read `blueprint.md` first; it is the contract and it supersedes everything else in
the repository, including this file. `README.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and
`ROADMAP.md` are derived from it and may lag it.

Two framings matter and they are different:

- **What the system does** — a public-data upstream analytics loop from raw
  regulator files to NPV, with audit-grade lineage on every number.
- **What the project is for** — measuring what is reproducible without proprietary
  data, and treating transparency as the trust mechanism a garage build actually
  has. The comparison against named commercial vendors is internal-only and gated
  behind an IP review (`blueprint.md` §8.2). Do not restate it as public
  positioning.

## The invariants worth knowing

- **No naked numbers.** Every served figure has a derivation handle. Untraceable equals wrong.
- **Strict layering.** Raw is immutable, staging is source-faithful and never serves, canonical is conformed, marts serve and never ingest.
- **Conformance as data (R8).** Every cross-source mapping decision is a row in `conformance_rules` served at `/conformance`, not a line of code.
- **Append-only memory.** Restatements are new events. Nothing upstream is edited in place.
- **API-10 is the identity spine.** API-14 normalises to it. One producing wellbore per API-10 is assumed; violations are quarantined and counted, not mis-joined.
- **Oil is the headline stream**, gas and water are secondary targets, GOR and water cut are derived surfaces and never model targets.
- **Inventory slots are not reserves.** No slot without geometric admissibility and a support score; no rollup without its spacing assumption stated.

## Designed API surface (not yet live)

```
GET  /wells/{api10}            GET  /wells/{api10}/production   GET  /wells/{api10}/analogs
POST /forecasts                POST /valuations                 POST /scenarios
POST /sensitivities            POST /inventory/runs             POST /wellsets
GET  /typecurves               GET  /operators/league           POST /aois
GET  /conformance              GET  /explain/{artifact_id}      GET  /recipes/{artifact_id}
GET  /quality/scorecard        GET  /quality/quarantine         GET  /audit
```

Any endpoint accepts `?explain=true`, which inlines the lineage block that the UI
drawer renders. There is no private endpoint behind the UI.

## Data sources

Public, keyless regulator and industry files only: North Dakota DMR (well-level
production, permits, surveys, tops), Texas Railroad Commission (PDQ lease
production, W-2/G-1 completions, W-1 permits, GIS well lines), New Mexico OCD
(well-level production), FracFocus (completion design), plus PLSS and spacing-unit
geography. Attribute the agency that publishes the file, not glasswell.

Texas reports at the lease level while ND and NM report at the well level. That
asymmetry is the allocation problem, and glasswell measures its error against two
independent validators rather than hiding it.

## Honest limits

Not mineral ownership. Not daily production. Not reserves. Not multi-tenant. Not an
OSDU implementation. Not investment advice. Every number derives from public
filings that states restate, and restatements are visible in the audit stream
rather than smoothed away.
